- Model consistently underestimates prices in early periods (first 5–10 days) and overestimates in late periods (last 5–10 days), suggesting a lag or horizon bias.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., 79.80 → 80.24), model forecasts overshoot and fail to correct downward quickly.
- Mean reversion is not captured: model holds high forecasts longer than actual price declines.
- Model exhibits persistent downward bias in the second half of the 30-day window, especially after 20–25 days.
- Forecasts tend to be too optimistic in the first 10 days, then too pessimistic in the last 10 days — suggesting a non-linear adjustment error.
- Model fails to account for recent price momentum; it lags behind actual trend reversals or accelerations.
- When true price drops sharply (e.g., 79.80 → 70.00), model does not adjust forecast downward sufficiently early — leading to persistent overestimation.
- Model underestimates the magnitude of price corrections after peaks — especially in the 20–30 day range.
